intro.heading: We get closer to understand what matters most to you.

story.heading: A business built through relationships.
paragraphs: Bright Fortune (Far East) Limited began operations in 1995. Its founder, Chander Lalwani, entered the insurance field in 1983.

Our work spans general, fire, marine, burglary, property all risks, life, medical and dental insurance for local and expatriate clients. Across those different needs, the starting point is a clear understanding of the client.
We aim to make the insurance conversation more useful: ask the right questions, explain relevant options and pay attention to the terms that can make a practical difference.

founder.name: Chander Lalwani
founder.bio: Chander Lalwani entered the insurance field in 1983 and founded Bright Fortune in 1995. The company’s published offering spans general, property, marine, life and health insurance, serving local and expatriate clients from Hong Kong. His career provides the historical foundation for a business focused on appropriate advice, product understanding and personal service.

intro.heading: Insurance around your circumstances.
paragraphs: A business asset, a shipment and a family’s income each raise different questions. The right starting point is understanding the exposure and what a policy would need to do.

Bright Fortune helps clients consider relevant options across its published areas of insurance. Our role is to bring the detail into focus, so that price, scope and conditions can be discussed together.

connected.heading: See how the pieces fit.
paragraphs: A company may need to consider property alongside marine interests. A family may want to discuss medical insurance alongside longer-term protection.
Bringing those needs into one conversation can help identify overlaps, changing priorities and questions that a single-product discussion may miss.

hero.title: Support when you need clarity.
hero.intro: Practical help with the information, communication and next steps involved in a claim.

intro.heading: A clear starting point.
paragraphs: If something has happened, refer first to your policy’s reporting requirements and any emergency assistance instructions. Contact the relevant emergency services if anyone is in immediate danger.

For a policy arranged through Bright Fortune, contact us with a brief account of the event and the policy details available. We can help identify the information needed and assist with communication as the claim progresses. The insurer assesses cover and any settlement under the policy.

steps.title: Tell us what happened
steps.body: Explain the date, location and nature of the event. Include your policy number if you have it, and tell us if there is an urgent reporting deadline.

steps.title: Keep the supporting information
steps.body: Retain relevant correspondence, receipts and photographs where safe and appropriate. We can help clarify what information the insurer may request.

steps.title: Follow the policy process
steps.body: Use any insurer notification or assistance channel required by your policy. Do not assume that a general website enquiry satisfies a policy deadline.

steps.title: Stay connected
steps.body: Keep a record of reference numbers and requests for further information. Tell us about material developments so we can help with the next steps.

faqs.question: Can I upload claim documents here?
faqs.answer: No. This website is for initial enquiries. Please do not enter identity documents, medical records, bank details or full claim files. Ask your broker or insurer for the appropriate document channel.

faqs.question: Does contacting Bright Fortune mean my claim is accepted?
faqs.answer: No. Cover and settlement depend on the policy and the insurer’s assessment. Acknowledging an enquiry does not confirm that a claim is covered.

faqs.question: What if the matter is urgent?
faqs.answer: Follow the emergency assistance and notification instructions in your policy immediately. The general website enquiry route is not an emergency service and does not replace insurer reporting requirements.
